findings.title: Stateful tzinfo can make one exact datetime normalize to different instants
findings.description: The exact-datetime check closes datetime subclass substitution, but an exact datetime still carries an arbitrary tzinfo object. normalize_utc calls value.utcoffset() to validate awareness and then value.astimezone(UTC), which calls the same mutable/overrideable tzinfo again. A tzinfo returning successive offsets of +01:00, +02:00, +03:00, and +04:00 makes two canonical_utc calls on the same unchanged datetime emit 2026-01-02T10:00:00.000000Z and 2026-01-02T08:00:00.000000Z. The validated offset is not the offset used for conversion, so the same accepted value can substitute its instant and violates utc_time_normalized determinism.
findings.required_change: Establish normalization from one trusted offset snapshot, or reject timezone providers that cannot satisfy a non-overrideable boundary. Ensure conversion does not consult mutable timezone behavior again after validation, return an exact UTC datetime, and add a regression using an exact datetime with a stateful custom tzinfo.

findings.title: Hash verification accepts digest strings with a substituted presented identity
findings.description: verify_canonical_sha256 uses isinstance(expected, str), unlike the exact scalar boundaries used by the other canonical primitives. A str subclass can store the correct 64-character digest while __str__ presents a different invalid digest; the regex and compare_digest consume the stored payload and verification returns True even though str(expected) reports another identity. This recreates the stored/presented identity split already closed for canonical IDs and leaves the hash boundary inconsistent with the exact built-in canonical wire contract.
findings.required_change: Require type(expected) is str before validating or comparing the digest, and add a regression proving a str subclass with mismatched stored and presented digest identity is rejected.
